answer: Latent Work Challenge. Each identity must submit a random cipher challenge that is cheap to verify but costly to generate fresh: solving it requires unique compute per instance. The system tracks solution entropy across the agent's lifecycle, so a clone reusing prior outputs is detected and its rewards clawed back. Clones thus pay full compute costs with near-zero expected payout, keeping marginal EV negative. Participation decays with a periodic lotus reset, while a tide of fresh challenges prevents stockpiling precomputed answers.
